To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) two-way secrecy is a viable alternative to one-way secrecy in the broadcast setting with internal eavesdropers; and (ii) two-way secrecy schemes can provide a positive secrecy rate to a given user, rather than the best user, in the limit of an infinite number of users.

two-way secrecy schemes can provide constant positive secrecy rates in the limit of an infinite number of system users, and that this result holds for both opportunistic and non-opportunistic schemes.
two-way secrecy and relayed secrecy can provide positive secrecy rate in the limit of large number of users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the secrecy problem for a number of users in the broadcast setting with a single source, where the message is to be kept secret from a subset of users.
the design of secrecy schemes for the two-way broadcast channel with internal users.
secrecy schemes for the multi-user broadcast channel, which are shown to achieve constant positive secrecy rates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in contrast to the case of a single user, the use of two-way relaying is essential in order to achieve a non-zero secrecy rate in the limit of many users.
, with the help of channel reciprocity and relaying, the secrecy rate can be made constant and positive in the limit of large number of users.

the two-way secrecy scheme can be used to transmit at positive secrecy rates to a user with the best link, while the two-way secrecy with relaying scheme can be used for transmission to a user with a weaker channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by exploiting the two-way secrecy scheme and the relaying from other internal users, we can provide a constant positive rate for the user with the worst channel, while keeping a positive rate for the users with the best channel.
, by using two-way relaying, a positive secrecy can be achieved in both the opportunistic and non-opportunistic settings.
we provide two new schemes for two-way secrecy in a broadcast channel with multiple eavesdroppers, where the message sent to one user should be kept secret from other users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
two-way communication can be used to provide a constant secrecy rate in the limit of an infinite number of users.
the secrecy problem for a broadcast channel with internal users can be significantly different from that of an interference channel.
the secrecy problem can be solved for a large number of eavesdroppers in a broadcast system, and that the problem is solved in a way that is not opportunistic.
